title: SDK migration utilities and streaming ergonomics — v1->v2 deprecations & changelog automation
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Goal: Ship an ergonomic migration and docs bundle that helps customers move from SDK v1 -> v2 (Python/TypeScript/Go). Deliverables: (1) migration guide (breaking changes, deprecations, recommended replacements), (2) streaming ergonomics guide per language, (3) retry semantics and idempotency guidance with examples, (4) automated changelog generation process that captures API surface changes and package release notes.
background: v2 SDKs introduce a few deliberate ergonomics changes: a unified streaming interface, stronger default retry/backoff behavior, and removal of legacy client constructors. Early beta feedback shows confusion around streaming usage patterns (especially for consumers migrating from callback-based or generator-based v1 APIs) and around how retries interact with streaming and function-calling flows. We also want to reduce manual work producing changelogs for each language when surface changes land in the monorepo.
proposal: 1) Publish language-specific migration guide pages in docs repo and link them in SDK packaging; include short code examples converting common patterns. 2) Add a compatibility helper module in each SDK (e.g., redwood.sdk.compat.v1_to_v2) that offers 'shim' helpers for top-5 breaking changes. 3) Standardize streaming primitives across languages: async iterator pattern for Python and TypeScript, channel/stream Reader for Go. 4) Define retry semantics as: idempotent-safe auto-retries (2 retries default with exponential backoff and jitter), and provide opt-out and custom retry hooks. 5) Implement a changelog automation action that parses code-level @deprecated annotations and CHANGELOG.md fragments, auto-generates release notes and a migration checklist for the docs site.
acceptance_criteria:
- Migration guide pages live and linked from SDK README for Python/TS/Go.
- Compatibility shim modules implemented with unit tests covering conversion cases.
- Streaming API examples added for common patterns (chat streaming, long-polling embeddings) across three languages.
- Retry default behavior implemented in each SDK with opt-out and configurable backoff; e2e test that simulates transient errors and validates not to double-invoke non-idempotent requests without explicit idempotency keys.
- Changelog action runs in CI and produces a draft release note artifact and a per-PR changelog blurb when @changelog tag is present.
- Docs and examples reviewed by PM and DevRel and merged.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Shims mask real breaking changes and delay migrations. Mitigation: limit shim surface to non-security-breaking convenience helpers and mark them deprecated with a 6-month removal window.
Risk: Retry behavior may cause duplicate operations (billing or side effects). Mitigation: Default to only auto-retry idempotent operations (generation/embeddings are idempotent by content key); non-idempotent routes require explicit idempotency key header or explicit 'retry: true' opt-in.
Risk: Changelog automation can miss context and produce low-quality notes. Mitigation: include a PR template requiring a 1-2 sentence 'migration note' if the PR changes public API; keep automated notes as drafts requiring human review before publish.
implementation_notes:
- Python: provide async iterator via 'stream = client.responses.stream(...)' and 'async for chunk in stream:' example. Include a small compat shim 'from redwood.sdk.compat import stream_v1_to_v2' for beta users.
- TypeScript: standardize on AsyncIterable<ResponseChunk> and provide RxJS interop helper in devtools. Example: 'for await (const part of client.stream(...)) { }'.
- Go: expose a StreamReader with Recv() and Close() methods, plus helper to convert to channel for idiomatic Go.
- Retries: centralize retry logic in core/http layer so all clients share identical backoff parameters. Use jittered exponential backoff: base=200ms, factor=2, max=5s, max_attempts default=3. Make these configurable via client options.
- Idempotency: encourage use of 'Idempotency-Key' header. When absent, SDK will default to only retry on safe endpoints. Document which endpoints are considered safe.
- Changelog automation: build a GitHub Action that scans modified packages for '@changelog' annotations in PR body or code comments. Output: artifacts/release-notes/draft-ENG-<key>.md and a docs/auto-migrations/<version>.md draft. Action should attach artifact and comment on PR with link.
examples:
Python streaming example:
>>> async with Client(api_key=SECRET) as c:
...     stream = c.chat.stream(model="redwood-stream-1", messages=conversation)
...     async for event in stream:
...         if event.type == 'delta':
...             print(event.delta)
...
TypeScript streaming example:
const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-stream-1', messages });
for await (const chunk of stream) { console.log(chunk.delta) }

Go streaming example:
stream, err := client.ChatStream(ctx, params)
for {
    chunk, err := stream.Recv()
    if err == io.EOF { break }
    if err != nil { return err }
    fmt.Println(chunk.Delta)
}

Retry usage example (Python):
client = Client(retries={ 'max_attempts': 4, 'base_backoff_ms': 150, 'max_backoff_ms': 4000 })
# For non-idempotent ops: attach idempotency_key to request or set retry_policy='manual'

Changelog annotation example (PR body):
- @changelog: "Renamed Client.create_stream -> Client.stream; added streaming iterator ergonomics. Migration note: replace create_stream(...) with stream(...)."
